findings.title: Reviewer output becomes executable shell authority

where.snippet:
- [ ] **C.5 Objective confirmation.** For `test`, `absence`, `path_exists`, and `path_changed`,
      the supervisor runs `verify_cmd` or checks `verify_paths` in the verify pane under the
      exit protocol. An unconfirmed blocking finding is demoted to `warning` and logged.

findings.detail: The grid explicitly forbids model-authored shell commands, but plan §2.2 requires a reviewer-supplied verify_cmd and C.5 executes it without a typed operand boundary or approved command mapping. A malicious diff that steers the reviewer can cause arbitrary commands to run with the verifier's permissions; the exit protocol authenticates completion, not command safety.
findings.fix: Replace verify_cmd with closed typed checks compiled by the supervisor into approved commands, and test rejection of shell syntax, path escapes, and unapproved operations.

findings.title: Confirmation errors silently remove blocking findings

where.task: merge-busybrain-herdr-plan.md / §2.2 / Where it sits in the lifecycle
where.snippet:
A blocking finding the
supervisor cannot confirm is logged and demoted to `warning`, which is BusyBrain's
`review_gate.py:44-64` rule and the one part of its review loop that reduced churn.

findings.detail: The rule makes no distinction between successfully disproving a finding and failing to run its confirmation because of a timeout, missing tool, malformed check, or inaccessible file. A candidate that causes the check to error can therefore turn a real blocker into a warning and proceed to land; C.5 repeats this behavior despite the grid flagging review failure-transition gaps.
findings.fix: Define confirmed, disproved, and indeterminate confirmation outcomes, and retain a blocking gate with bounded retry or escalation for indeterminate outcomes.

findings.title: Review verdict is not bound to the candidate that lands

where.snippet:
- [ ] **C.4 The API call.** One Messages request with the schema as the tool input schema. The
      reviewer receives the goal, the diff against `origin/<base_branch>`, and the verifier
      output. A test asserts the worker transcript is not in the request.

findings.detail: The grid requires review and verification to share one immutable candidate, but §2.2 uses origin/<base_branch>..HEAD and C.4 records neither immutable endpoints nor a verdict-to-candidate binding. Although §2.9 pins transfer and final test commits, it never makes an existing review invalid after candidate changes, so an edited candidate can reuse approval of an earlier diff.
findings.fix: Capture immutable base and candidate commits plus verification-policy hash before review, bind the verdict to that tuple, and reject landing or integration when any component changes.

findings.title: Pane workers have no specified per-call quota enforcement boundary

where.snippet:
- [ ] **H.3 Reserve estimated use before every model call.** Admission and reservation happen
      in one SQLite transaction. Completion settles actual use. An unknown billed timeout retains
      its reservation until reconciliation.

findings.detail: The plan runs workers in agent CLI panes with any of 23 kinds, while only the reviewer is a daemon-owned API request. Assuming a worker CLI initiates its own model requests, no plan section or TODO item supplies interception or credential mediation that forces those calls through H.3; a worker or its child can continue spending after the pool pauses without acquiring reservations. Supervisor-visible actor records and a packet prohibition on unmanaged children do not establish that admission boundary.
findings.fix: Specify and test an enforceable provider-call adapter or gateway for supported worker kinds, and restrict unattended quota enforcement claims to workers whose calls pass through it.

root_cause_groups.summary: Reviewer-generated commands cross into verifier execution without constrained operands.
An inability to confirm is treated as evidence that a blocker can be removed.
Review approval lacks immutable candidate identity enforced at landing.
Per-call reservations lack a specified mediation boundary for pane-hosted CLIs.
